title: The creed, reviewed

cards: Facing east or facing west, says a verse in surah al-Baqarah, is not what righteousness is.

Then it says what is, in paraphrase: believing in Allah and the Last Day, the angels, the scripture and the prophets, and giving wealth, out of love, to relatives, orphans, the needy and the traveler.

A creed and a kindness in one breath, neither left waiting for the other. This year the creed came most often from a different scene: a stranger who walks in and asks questions. Today, six articles of faith.

teach.b: In the hadith of Jibril in Sahih Muslim, a stranger in white sits knee to knee with the Prophet, peace be upon him, and asks: what is faith?
The answer, in paraphrase: to believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers and the Last Day, and to believe in the decree, its good and its bad. Six.
The Qur'an says something close about the believers: "Each one believeth in Allah and His angels and His scriptures and His messengers." What do the six share?
Each reaches past what the eye can check. Nobody at that gathering could point to an angel, open the Last Day, or hold the decree in a hand.
The creed is a map of what lies past the eye: the One, the messengers between, the books they carried, and the road ahead.

teach.h: REASONED IN MORE THAN ONE WAY.
teach.b: Theologians reasoned about these six, and not all the same way. The Ash'ari and Maturidi schools defended the creed with arguments.

teach.h: IT WAS JIBRIL, TEACHING BY ASKING.
teach.b: The Athari approach took the texts as they came, without asking how. Twelver Shia teaching arranges its roots of faith in its own way, naming oneness, justice, prophethood, the imamate and the return.

The year described them side by side and ranked none. And the end of the scene. When the stranger leaves, the Prophet later tells Umar, in paraphrase, that it was Jibril, who came to teach them their religion.
So the questions were the lesson.

how: Muslims learn the articles of faith from the hadith of Jibril and the Qur'an, and teachers explain each one; theological schools reason about them in different ways.

games.q: a friend asks you, over lunch, what Muslims believe. in the hadith of Jibril, how does the answer go?
o: the five pillars: testimony, prayer, zakat, fasting, pilgrimage.
Allah, His angels, books, messengers, the Last Day, and the decree.
games.why: in Sahih Muslim, the pillars answer "what is Islam?"; the six answer "what is faith?"

practice: One to a breath, let the six go by, quietly or in your head: Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and the decree, its good and its bad.
If these are your faith, you can say them as your own; if you're learning, just hear the list the way the companions heard it, from someone else's mouth. Then rest in the quiet after the sixth.
